issues.legal_issue: A defendant may maintain a counterclaim for injunction in a suit for injunction even when the counterclaim arises from an independent cause of action or concerns different property, subject to the applicable timing and jurisdictional limits.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sued for a perpetual injunction concerning property they claimed to possess.
The defendants asserted possession of other land and counterclaimed for an injunction against interference with their possession of that land.
The plaintiffs disputed the counterclaim and applied to have it excluded from the written statement.
The trial court refused to exclude the counterclaim, and the High Court directed the trial court to determine whether the properties were identical.
The Supreme Court held that a different property or independent cause of action did not make the counterclaim inadmissible and dismissed the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The counterclaim was maintainable in the injunction suit, even if it concerned different property or an independent cause of action, and could be tried with the original claim.
issues.legal_principle: Order 8 Rules 6A to 6G of the Code of Civil Procedure authorize a defendant to bring a counterclaim for any right or claim arising from a cause of action against the plaintiff, including one independent of the plaintiff’s cause of action, provided the cause of action accrued before the defendant delivered the defence or the time to do so expired and the counterclaim is within the court’s pecuniary jurisdiction. Under Rule 6A(2), the counterclaim has the effect of a cross-suit, and under Rule 6A(4) it is treated as a plaint. Rule 6C provides a means to seek exclusion of a counterclaim. The Court relied on Laxmidas Dahyabhai Kabarwala v. Nanabhai Chunilal Kabarwala, which recognized that a counterclaim may be treated as a cross-suit and decided in the same proceedings, and Mahendra Kumar v. State of Madhya Pradesh, which held a counterclaim maintainable where its cause of action arose before the written statement was filed.

predicates.civil_suit_with_defendant_counterclaim: A defendant asserted a claim against the plaintiff in an existing civil suit.
predicates.counterclaim_cause_accrued_in_time: The cause underlying the defendant’s claim accrued before the defendant delivered the defence or the time to deliver it expired.
predicates.counterclaim_within_court_value_limit: The value of the defendant’s counterclaim was within the court’s pecuniary jurisdiction.
predicates.counterclaim_may_be_adjudicated_with_ori: The defendant’s counterclaim may be heard and decided together with the plaintiff’s claim.

issues.definition: When a defendant asserts a counterclaim in a civil suit and its cause accrued in time and falls within the court’s value limit, the counterclaim may be adjudicated with the original suit.
